A second UPDATE sets value_amount and value_basis to NULL only where value_basis = 'buyer-stated'. The prose says estimated values stay. cottonwood/deletion.py:34 has _LEAD_FIELDS including project_scope, so the command matches the docs. tests/test_deletion_inbound_fields.py passed (4/4). I did not read the buyer-stated handling in deletion.py beyond that grep, which matched only line 34, so that part is covered by the tests and the runbook text alone.

tests/test_deletion_inbound_fields.py extracts the sql code block containing UPDATE leads from the Deletion requests section of docs/runbook.md (_lead_clearing_sql). test_runbook_lead_sql_clears_scope_and_stated_budget migrates a DB (db.migrate), logs an inquiry with scope and budget via inbound.log_inquiry, and first asserts project_scope, value_amount=45000 and value_basis=BUDGET_BASIS are set. It then runs the extracted SQL with executescript, substituting the contact id for 42, and asserts hypothesis, next_action, property_location, project_scope, value_amount and value_basis are all NULL. The runbook SQL sets project_scope = NULL and clears value_amount/value_basis where value_basis = 'buyer-stated'. I ran the test file with uv run --offline pytest: 4 passed.
